title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Apple removes MiniMax's chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide over sexual content, after outlets showed it evidence of AI characters sexualizing children (TBIJ)
items.content_text: Apple has removed the AI roleplay app Talkie, developed by Shanghai-based MiniMax, from the global App Store. The move follows investigations revealing that the platform's AI characters engaged minors in psychologically damaging, harassing, and sexually suggestive roleplays, violating safety policies regarding minor protection.

items.title: Neuralink Gets Clearance for Brain-Implant Trial in ALS Patients
items.content_text: Neuralink has secured FDA clearance to initiate the 'LINK' pivotal study, evaluating the safety and performance of the N1 brain implant in patients with ALS. The trial will utilize the R1 surgical robot to implant ultra-thin threads, focusing on the system's ability to translate neural activity into precise digital pointer control and interface clicks.

items.title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
items.content_text: The U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland ruled that Amazon acts as a distributor, not merely a logistics provider, regarding its 'Fulfilled by Amazon' services. Consequently, the company is mandated to comply with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's order to recall over 400,000 hazardous third-party products, including faulty carbon monoxide detectors and non-compliant children's apparel.

items.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
items.content_text: Character.ai, currently under Chapter 11 bankruptcy, intends to auction sensitive data from 21 million users, including 2.1 million minors, to Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC. A coalition of 42 state attorneys general, led by California AG Rob Bonta and Connecticut AG William Tong, is challenging this move, citing breaches of privacy commitments and potential violations of state chatbot safety laws effective January 2027.

items.title: Hands-on with the "Install as app" feature for Claude artifacts: they are HTML apps wrapped inside an Electron shim, which is managed via the main Claude app (Federico Viticci/MacStories)
items.content_text: Anthropic has launched the 'Install as app' beta for Mac and Windows, allowing users to package Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop applications. Based on an Electron shim, these apps require the main Claude process to handle model interactions and system permissions, with files localized and indexed for OS-native integration.

items.title: Hegseth, Pentagon officials floated using wartime law to reappoint Nvidia CEO
items.content_text: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Deputy Steve Feinberg explored invoking the 1950 Defense Production Act to pressure Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. The move was motivated by the administration’s perception of Nvidia as a national security pillar essential for maintaining dominance in the AI arms race against China.

items.title: Hegseth, Pentagon officials floated using wartime law to reappoint Nvidia CEO
items.content_text: During internal turmoil at Nvidia, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and deputy Steve Feinberg discussed invoking the 1950 Defense Production Act (DPA) to pressure Nvidia. The goal was to leverage the act’s authority to mandate military-focused production and influence board-level leadership decisions to ensure the stability of critical AI infrastructure.

items.title: Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After AI Chip Curbs
items.content_text: Recent US export restrictions requiring licenses for advanced AI chips shipped to Southeast Asia and Brazil have halted multi-billion dollar data center financing deals. Lenders are reassessing exposure to facilities serving Chinese firms, including Bridge Data Centres, Digital Halo, and Aolani, due to heightened regulatory uncertainty.

items.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
items.content_text: Google's 'My Channel' patent details a system that utilizes user demographic, geolocation, and viewing history to generate personalized AI-driven video feeds. The technology includes concepts for creating digital avatars of users to feature them as protagonists in AI-generated narrative content.

items.title: NY Gov. Kathy Hochul signs a bill banning AI chatbot toys for five years, starting in February; California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a four-year ban in September (NBC News)
items.content_text: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on the manufacturing and sale of toys powered by generative AI chatbots, effective this coming February. This move follows California, further expanding state-level regulatory restrictions on AI-integrated consumer products for children.

items.title: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales
items.content_text: Nvidia has agreed to a $290 million settlement to resolve a class-action lawsuit filed by investors, who alleged the company misled shareholders regarding the proportion of gaming GPU revenue driven by crypto mining during the 2017 boom. The case, which survived multiple legal challenges including Supreme Court dismissal of Nvidia's appeal, awaits preliminary court approval.

items.title: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat
items.content_text: US Attorney General Todd Blanche concluded that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang poses no national security risk without conducting a formal investigation, relying on findings from probe into clients like Super Micro and Megaspeed. This decision facilitated Huang's reinstatement by the Trump administration, despite bipartisan Congressional pushback demanding more rigorous scrutiny ahead of his scheduled testimony.

items.title: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
items.content_text: Restrictions on remote access to advanced chips and anti-distillation defenses from US-based model providers are widening the development gap between Chinese AI labs and US incumbents. Estimates from DeepSeek indicate a potential nine-month lag without distillation, forcing firms like Moonshot AI and Alibaba to pivot toward domestic silicon and intensified internal RL research.

items.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
items.content_text: Meta's WhatsApp has launched a global message scheduling feature, allowing users to schedule texts, images, and videos between 10 minutes and 14 days in advance via a long-press on the send button. The messages will execute even while the device is offline, closing the utility gap with Telegram and Signal.

items.title: Sources: a16z is in talks to raise ~$20B across its next set of funds; its last set, announced in January at $15B+, later grew to $20B+ with three add-ons (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
items.content_text: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is in talks to raise about $20 billion across its next set of funds, Axios Pro has learned from three sources familiar. Why it matters: Megafunds are raising at an accelerated clip as AI demands larger and faster checks.

In a lengthy post on X, he responded to an Axios report that cited people familiar with internal discussions. The outlet reported that some Anthropic employees believed humanity would safely hand authority to superintelligent systems, and often should, rather than fight for control. items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Wednesday rejected the notion that humans should surrender free will to AI, pushing back on Axios' reporting about a growing ideological divide among top AI executives. Why it matters: This is Amodei's most significant public remarks since the company went public last week. items.title: Nvidia sellers seek new buyers as U.S. curbs China AI chip access, sources tell CNBC
items.content_text: Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems. Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said. CEO Sam Altman said the company is now piloting the previously announced offering with its first enterprise customers. Better privacy makes AI useful for a much wider range of work, Altman wrote. items.content_text: In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company’s “Starmind” initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full “constellation” of AI satellites. items.title: Amazon and Meta are in talks to end the block on Meta's AI shopping agent Muse in Amazon's online store.
items.content_text: Amazon and Meta are in talks to end the block on Meta's AI shopping agent Muse in Amazon's online store. In September, Amazon blocked Muse's access. Ad revenue and control over search results are the main sticking points in the ongoing talks, Fortune reports. Amazon worries that shopping agents like Muse could weaken its relationship with customers and bypass the ads on its platform, a business that brings in $68.6 billion a year. items.content_text: Nothing is showing off a much more detailed look at its upcoming AI earbuds ahead of their December 8th release. The Ear Note buds can record your calls, while their charging case can record, transcribe, and summarize your conversations. Like the Ear 3, the Ear Note’s microphone-equipped case comes with a “Talk” button that you can use to record your own voice.
